# Signal — Bugs & Findings

Lightweight catalog of bugs, defects, and verified findings for Signal itself.
Markdown-native by design — GitHub Issues are deferred until Signal has live
users (see `FUTURE-IDEAS.md` § "GitHub Issues for work-item tracking — deferred").

**Discipline** (per the "always catalog bugs" norm): catalog a finding the moment
it surfaces → **triage** (read the code / confirm the root cause) → mark
**confirmed** or **dismissed**. Never graduate a finding to a confirmed bug
unverified.

- **Status:** `needs-triage` · `confirmed` · `dismissed` · `fixed`
- **Priority:** `P1` ship-blocker · `P2` should-fix · `P3` nice-to-have
- **Scope:** defects + verified findings only. Architectural ideas → `FUTURE-IDEAS.md`;
  design questions → `OPEN-QUESTIONS.md`; decisions → `DECISIONS.md`.

| B1 | `dismissed` | — | **`/sig:checkpoint` "Epic-ID-as-task-ID" + "only 2 of 5 commits".** Non-bug (triaged 2026-06-06). `isStateStale` deliberately filters the commit walk to `STATE_AFFECTING_PATHS` (`state.js:583`, D6 — editing future-ideas / decisions / milestone files is metadata curation, excluded by design), so 2-of-5 counting is correct. `TASK_ID_RE` (`checkpoint.js:25`) intentionally matches every hierarchy level, so `taskIdsInCommits` can include Epic/milestone IDs — harmless: it only filters `current_tasks`, which holds full task IDs. Surfaced from unverified surface behavior during a `markFresh` detour; reading the source dismissed it. |
| B51 | `fixed` | **P2** | **`discuss.md` still instructs the DISCUSS close to set `phase: PLAN`, which makes `/sig:plan`'s at-entry transition record PLAN as complete before PLAN has run.** `commands/discuss.md:158-161` ends with *"Update `STATE.md`: `## Current Phase` / `PLAN`"* — the pre-M5.E9 convention, where the **outgoing** command advanced the phase. M5.E9's `B41` fix moved that responsibility to the **incoming** command: `commands/plan.md:44` now says *"Before any Workflow step, call `await transitionPhase(baseDir, 'PLAN')` … It appends the phase being **left** to `completed_phases`."* **Both instructions survive, and obeying both writes a false entry.** If DISCUSS sets `phase: PLAN`, then at `/sig:plan` entry `leaving` resolves to **PLAN**, so `recordPhase` appends `PLAN (date)` — recording PLAN complete **before it did any work**. `recordPhase` is **deliberately append-only with no dedupe** (`state.js:425-427`, D-M5E9-5 / `B44` — a genuine re-transition did happen twice), so the false entry is **permanent** and later sits beside the real `PLAN (date)` appended when EXECUTE transitions. **Same family as `B48`:** an instruction whose literal execution corrupts the ledger M5.E9 built to make honest, while ignoring it is the only correct move. **Found by dogfooding — M5.E13's own DISCUSS, 2026-07-28.** The instruction was not obeyed; `phase` was left at `DISCUSS` so `/sig:plan` records the transition itself, which is the post-`B41` design. **Scope check: `discuss.md` is the sibling case of the four commands `B48` covers** — M5.E9 updated the four *incoming* commands and left the *outgoing* instruction in the fifth. `calibrate.md` and `ship.md` also called `transitionPhase` pre-M5.E9 and need the same read. **Folded into M5.E13 FR1** rather than opened as separate work: one instruction family, one fix. **→ Status reconciled 2026-08-02** (fix lane, BUGS.md status-vs-code sweep): fixed in **M5.E13** and never flipped. `commands/discuss.md:158` now reads **"Do NOT set `phase: PLAN` here"** — the incoming command advances the phase, not the outgoing one. Pinned by `tests/commands-wording.test.js:61`, which asserts no command sets a phase the next command also sets. |
| B52 | `fixed` (v0.1.20) | **P1** | **A Claude Code session binds to ONE plugin-cache version for its whole life, so Signal-on-Signal can dogfood a release two versions behind the repo — and it silently destroyed M5.E8's phase ledger.** Observed live 2026-07-28 at M5.E13 PLAN entry. `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, `package.json` and `marketplace.json` all read **0.1.13** (pinned to `8d20193`), a **0.1.13 cache exists and is correct** (`cache/signal/sig/0.1.13/commands/plan.md` has both `transitionPhase` refs), **yet the session loaded every `/sig:` command and every `tools/lib` module from `cache/signal/sig/0.1.11/`** — two releases behind. **The damage:** `setCurrentEpic` rolling `M5.E8 → M5.E13` ran **0.1.11's `state.js`**, which has **zero** references to `archivePhaseLog`/`partitionCompletedPhases` (repo has 6) because it predates M5.E9. The Epic-roll therefore reset `completed_phases` **without the archive-before-reset step M5.E9 added specifically to prevent this** — M5.E8's six-phase DISCUSS→SHIP run was **discarded with no error, no warning, and no record**. Proven by the sibling case sitting beside it: `.planning/archive/M5/E9/STATE-NARRATIVE.md` **exists** (written by the real tool on 2026-07-27, when M5.E8 opened under v0.1.12 code), while `.planning/archive/M5/E8/` **did not exist at all**. **Recovered** verbatim from `git show aff4098:.planning/STATE.md` into `archive/M5/E8/STATE-NARRATIVE.md`, zero entries lost — recoverable **only** because `.planning/` is tracked in git. **Why this outranks the bug it reproduced:** `B44` was *"a silent write that drops data"* and M5.E9 fixed it; this is that same loss re-entering through the **install layer**, where no amount of correct repo code prevents it. **It also corrupts dogfooding evidence in both directions** — a fixed bug can appear live (the stale cache still has it) and a live bug can appear fixed. Every `/sig:` command run in this session, including the `/sig:discuss` that opened M5.E13, was **v0.1.11 text**. **Fix shape (two halves):** (1) a session-start version check comparing the resolved plugin-cache path against `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, warning loudly on mismatch — cheap, deterministic, and the half that matters; (2) decide whether `setCurrentEpic` should refuse to reset a non-empty `completed_phases` it did not archive, which would have made this loud instead of silent regardless of version. **Note the shape:** the guard that would have caught it existed and was correct — it just wasn't the code that ran. That is the `B39`/`B46`/`I2` class arriving by a new route, which is why it belongs in **M5.E13**. **ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED 2026-07-28 — a mid-session auto-update race, not a broken install.** `installed_plugins.json` is **correct** (`installPath: …/sig/0.1.13`, `version: 0.1.13`) and `known_marketplaces.json` has **`autoUpdate: true`**. The plugin's `lastUpdated` is **`2026-07-28T13:38:41Z`**; this session had already started (its SessionStart hook reported STATE as of `13:37:23`). **Claude Code resolves the plugin path once at session start and holds it for the session's life**, so a session that began ~78 seconds before the auto-update kept **0.1.11** while every config file on disk correctly read 0.1.13. **Reproduced by Brett in a second, unrelated repo the same day** — it is **per-session, not per-project**: any session alive across an auto-update keeps the version it started with. **Not Signal-specific in mechanism** (it affects any Claude Code plugin) **but severe for Signal specifically**, because Signal's tools mutate project state, so a stale binding does not merely behave oddly — it writes with retired code paths. **Immediate remedy: restart the CLI process. A context clear (`/clear`) is very likely NOT sufficient — and the distinction matters, because "restart the session" is ambiguous between exactly those two things.** *Reasoned, not verified:* plugin resolution builds the command/skill registry, which is **process-level** state; `/clear` resets conversation context without restarting the process, so the resolved paths should survive it. A marketplace refresh that re-fetches without rebuilding the in-process registry should likewise not help. **Decisive 10-second test, because every `/sig:` command prints its own version in its text** (this session's `/sig:resume` opened by citing `…/sig/0.1.11/tools/lib/profile.js`): run `/clear`, then `/sig:status`, and read the cited path — `0.1.13` means a clear re-resolves, `0.1.11` means only a full process restart does. **Nothing in config needs repair either way.** **→ SECOND LIVE SIGHTING 2026-08-02, and this one delivered a retired instruction rather than destroying data.** Caught at the top of `/sig:discuss --epic M5.E18`: the skill text the session loaded cites `…/cache/signal/sig/**0.1.13**/skills/define/…`, while `installed_plugins.json` records `installPath: …/sig/**0.1.15**`, `version: 0.1.15`, `lastUpdated: 2026-08-01T18:13:18Z`. **Config on disk is correct and the session is still two releases behind it.** **CORRECTION, same day, before anyone acted on it:** this row first said the timing *"differs from the originating case"* and that the mechanism was *"not yet explained."* **Both were wrong, and wrong the same way — I read the session transcript's creation time as the process's start time.** `ps` says otherwise: the CLI process serving this session (**pid 86260**, cwd `…/dev-biz/signal`) started **Tue Jul 28 17:29**, when v0.1.13 *was* the current release. It has been alive **five days**. The session id was minted Aug 2 12:50 by a `/clear` **inside that same process**. So this is the originating mechanism exactly — *a session alive across an auto-update keeps the version it started with* — with a **four-day** window instead of 78 seconds. **And it converts this row's own open hypothesis into a measurement.** The row said, marked *reasoned, not verified*: *"A context clear is very likely NOT sufficient … `/clear` resets conversation context without restarting the process, so the resolved paths should survive it."* **Verified now:** a `/clear` ran at 12:50, the process kept its 0.1.13 binding, and the very next `/sig:` command cited `…/sig/0.1.13/`. Delete the *reasoned-not-verified* caveat — restart is required, clear is not enough, observed. **The generalisation that matters more than either:** a long-lived process is the common case, not the edge one. `ps` at the same moment found **five** live CLI processes — `elicitation-engine` (Jul 25), `eval-project-J` (Jul 25), `eval-project-C` (Jul 28), `signal` (Jul 28), `eval-project-A` (Aug 2) — so **four of five were running machinery 5 to 8 days old**, against real projects, with nothing anywhere saying so. The originating incident read as a freak 78-second race; it is not. It is the default state of any editor left open over a weekend. **The damage this time:** v0.1.13's `discuss.md` still carries the exact block `B51` deleted — *"Update `STATE.md`: `## Current Phase` / `PLAN`"* — so an agent following the text it was handed would have written the permanent false `PLAN (date)` entry `B51` exists to prevent (`completed_phases` is append-only with no dedupe, `D-M5E9-5`, so it cannot be undone by a later correct run). Diffed live: cached 174 lines vs repo 170; the four extra lines *are* the retired instruction. **So the row's prediction — "a fixed bug can appear live" — is now observed, and it is worse than stated: the stale cache does not merely fail to deliver a fix, it actively re-issues the instruction the fix removed.** **Also measured:** there is **no `0.1.16` cache at all** (`0.1.5, 0.1.6, 0.1.8–0.1.11, 0.1.13, 0.1.15`), so even a correctly-bound session runs one release behind `main` until the marketplace re-fetches — expected, given `source: "."` means users track `main` and the cache refreshes on update, but it means **Signal-on-Signal always dogfoods older machinery than it just merged.** **Consequence for the Epic:** `M5.E18` was NOT opened in this session — no `setCurrentEpic`, no `transitionPhase`, no artifacts written. Running a Signal-on-Signal Epic on retired command text corrupts exactly the dogfooding evidence the Epic exists to gather. **This strengthens fix half (1)** — a session-start check comparing the resolved cache path against the install record — from *cheap and deterministic* to *the only thing that would have caught either sighting*; both were found by a human noticing a version string in passing. **→ THIRD LIVE SIGHTING 2026-08-03, at a `/sig:resume` that had just been restarted for the second one.** The command text loaded cites `…/cache/signal/sig/**0.1.16**/tools/lib/…` while `installed_plugins.json` records `installPath: …/sig/**0.1.17**`, `version: 0.1.17`. **No damage:** Signal's own `phase: DISCUSS` is canonical, so 0.1.16's pre-`B70` `nextActionForPhase` returned `/sig:plan` rather than throwing — verified by executing it, not assumed. **But the near-miss is the point:** v0.1.17 *is* the `B70` fix, so the identical stale binding on any of the **5 of 12** projects with a non-canonical `phase` takes out the whole briefing. **And it corrects a measurement in this row.** The second-sighting text asserts *"there is **no** `0.1.16` cache at all"* and concludes that Signal-on-Signal therefore *"always dogfoods older machinery than it just merged."* The first half has expired — the cache directory now holds `0.1.5, 0.1.8–0.1.11, 0.1.13, 0.1.15, **0.1.16**, **0.1.17**`, so the marketplace re-fetch does land. The second half survives for a different reason: **the fetch lands on disk and the running process still does not see it.** That is a sharper claim than the one it replaces, and it removes the only explanation that made this look self-limiting. **Sighting cadence is now the strongest argument for fix half (1):** three sightings in six days (07-28, 08-02, 08-03), each found by a human reading a version string in passing, and the interval is shrinking while the version gap narrows — a smaller gap is *harder* to notice, not easier. **→ FIXED in v0.1.20, both halves, in the fix lane.** Half 1 is `tools/lib/plugin-binding.js`: it compares the plugin copy **the process actually resolved** — derived from the module's own path via `import.meta.url`, never `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT`, because the env var states where the plugin is *supposed* to be and this bug is exactly that disagreement — against what `installed_plugins.json` records, and renders a banner naming both versions, both paths, and the one remedy. **Wired at two surfaces, and the second is not optional:** the SessionStart hook (`hooks/warn-stale-plugin-binding.js`) **structurally cannot see the originating sighting** — the binding is resolved before the hook runs, so a mid-session auto-update is invisible to it, and the 78-second race would still be silent. `/sig:status` and `/sig:resume` re-read both files **at the moment of use**, which is the only moment that can observe an update that landed after binding. A hook-only fix would have covered the case that mostly is not the bug. **False-positive gate:** a bound root outside `~/.claude/plugins/cache/` is a local checkout and stays silent, or Signal-on-Signal would banner itself from the moment `cut-release.js` bumps a branch. **Inherent limit, stated so nobody tests it wrong:** the check ships inside the cache copy it inspects, so it cannot fire until a session binds to a version that has it. **Half 2 is the `setCurrentEpic` guard, and building it found the bug was wider than this row said.** The row framed the ledger loss as a stale-cache consequence; it is not — the reset is unconditional, so *"archive first"* was a step that could be skipped rather than an invariant that held, and **three** branches reached the zeroing write with an unarchived log while only one was covered. Two are reachable with no stale cache at all: a **linear** project opening its first Epic never entered the archive branch, and `epicArchiveDirFor` returned null for any non-strict `current_epic` — `PHASE11`, measured live in eval-project-C by `B53` — whereupon the caller read that null as *"skip the archive"* and reset anyway. Now: linear history archives to `.planning/STATE-HISTORY.md` (the destination `completePhase`'s trim already uses), non-strict-but-safe units get M5.E18's flat per-unit directory, and a log with **no** safe destination **throws before any write** — pinned by a test asserting STATE.md is byte-identical after the refusal, not merely that it threw. 2233 → **2269 tests**.

  **⚠ Related hazard, unobserved — flagged as a risk, not a finding.** `~/.claude/plugins/.last_inuse_sweep` (last run `2026-07-28T00:41:11Z`) indicates a periodic prune of cached plugin versions, and the cache currently holds **seven** (`0.1.5`, `0.1.6`, `0.1.8`, `0.1.9`, `0.1.10`, `0.1.11`, `0.1.13`). If that sweep removes a version it considers unused **while a session is still bound to it**, that session loses its command surface mid-flight — and a Signal session losing `tools/lib` mid-Epic is worse than one running stale code, because partial writes become possible. `0.1.11` is intact today (18 commands present), so **this has not happened and is not claimed to have happened.** It is the same shape as the binding bug itself: **a live reference that nothing else knows is live.** Worth confirming the sweep's in-use detection accounts for open sessions before treating the multi-version cache as harmless. **Separate observation, uncertain significance:** that same record carries `gitCommitSha: a73d550`, which is *"M4.t19: marketplace install layout fix + plugin slug signal→sig (v0.1.0)"* — a **v0.1.0-era commit**, unchanged since `installedAt: 2026-05-14` while `lastUpdated` has moved across thirteen releases. Whether that field is meant to track the release or the original install is **not established**; flagged rather than claimed, since a third disagreeing version statement is exactly `B49`'s shape and should not be asserted from a guess. |
| B53 | `fixed` | **P2** | **A non-strict `current_epic` splits artifact WRITE naming from READ resolution, so a phase command can write `1-PLAN.md` while the next command reads a stale `PHASE11-PLAN.md` — and `references/epic-native-flow.md` states the opposite as a guarantee.** Two seams read the same field with **different regexes**: `artifactName` (`resume.js`) uses the **strict** shape and fails open to *linear* naming (documented at `epic-native-flow.md:44`), while `resolveArtifactPath` (`resume.js:30`) uses the **lenient** `EPIC_ID_RE = /^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$/` and places the Epic-prefixed candidate **first** in its candidate list — so an existing `{value}-{ARTIFACT}.md` **shadows** a freshly written `1-{ARTIFACT}.md`, which is checked only afterward. **`epic-native-flow.md:31` claims they cannot diverge:** *"They are symmetric — whatever `artifactName` emits, `resolveArtifactPath` with the same opts resolves back."* **True for a strict Epic ID; false for every non-strict value.** **Verified by execution** against the installed v0.1.13 with `eval-project-C`'s real STATE value: `artifactName('PLAN', {currentEpic:'PHASE11'})` → **`1-PLAN.md`**; `resolveArtifactPath(…, 'PLAN', {currentEpic:'PHASE11'})` → **`PHASE11-PLAN.md`**. With `M5.E9` both agree (`M5.E9-PLAN.md`). **Live field case:** `eval-project-C` carries `current_epic: PHASE11` — `detectMode` → **linear**, `setCurrentEpic` would have **rejected** it (it re-validates the strict shape), so it entered by a direct STATE write, the one path nothing validates. Its artifacts are all named `PHASE11-*.md`, so **reads work today only because the lenient regex matches**; the first `/sig:` command to *write* an artifact forks the naming and the write is then invisible to the next read. **The divergence is unobservable:** `detectMode` is named in exactly **one** command file (`ship.md`) — `/sig:status` and `/sig:resume` never print the detected mode, so a project reads as Epic to a human and linear to Signal with nothing saying so. **Secondary hazard, inferred from the instruction text and NOT measured** (it is agent-executed prose — M5.E8's exact subject): `ship.md` §0.5 derives `MILESTONE-{n}.md` from `current_epic`; `eval-project-C` has **no milestone file of any name** (verified), so an agent that eyeballs `PHASE11` as "Epic mode" rather than computing `detectMode` halts one step *before* `shipFR1Check` runs. **Origin — and it is a `B50` sighting.** Found while checking a `eval-project-C` session's claim that *"`shipFR1Check` halts with `NO_CURRENT_EPIC` on this project, which has never used Epics."* **That claim is false, on both the installed version and the one before it:** `PHASE11` is **truthy**, so the pre-`B42` `!state.current_epic` branch never fired either — executed, v0.1.13 → `{halt:false, skipped:true, reason:'linear mode …'}` and v0.1.11 → `{halt:false, skipped:true, reason:'not an Epic-close SHIP …'}`. The claim was composed from the *shape* of the situation ("no Epics → `NO_CURRENT_EPIC`") rather than from the artifact — **`B50`'s class, sighted in a downstream project rather than in Signal's own docs.** **Fix shape, three parts:** (1) a **`/sig:sweep` check for a set-but-non-strict `current_epic`**, naming what is therefore inactive — **shippable where M5.E9's removed phase-log check was not, and the distinction is the whole argument: the evidence here is *in the file* and mechanically testable against `EPIC_ID_STRICT_RE`, so it cannot false-positive on a healthy project**, whereas a past history-collapse was undetectable because the bug destroyed its own evidence; (2) **surface the detected mode** in `/sig:status` and `/sig:resume`; (3) **decide whether the two regexes should agree** — a design call, not a typo: the lenient one is load-bearing for existing non-strict projects' *reads*, so tightening it silently breaks them. **P2, not P1:** no data loss observed and reads currently resolve — but this is a silent stale-read path, and the same *"two layers, one field, opposite verdicts"* shape `B42` was closed on. **→ Status reconciled 2026-08-02** (fix lane, BUGS.md status-vs-code sweep): the defect is fixed in **M5.E13 (S1.t1)** and was never flipped. The write/read split is closed **by construction**: `resolveArtifactPath`'s first candidate *is* `artifactName(artifact, {currentEpic})` (Pattern W, `tools/lib/resume.js:64`), so neither seam guesses at the other's Epic-ID regex — `references/epic-native-flow.md:33` was rewritten to claim symmetry by construction rather than by convention, and `tests/resolve-artifact.test.js:166` pins it. Fix-shape part (1) shipped separately as M5.E16's sweep check `(h)` `epic-id-not-strict` (`tools/lib/state-drift.js:617`). **Residual, deliberately left open:** fix-shape part (2) — *surface the detected mode in `/sig:status` and `/sig:resume`* — is **not** implemented; `detectMode` is still called by no renderer (only referenced in a comment at `tools/lib/resume.js:146`), so a non-strict project still reads as Epic mode to a human and linear to Signal with nothing saying so. Tracked as `B68`. |
| B63 | `fixed` (v0.1.18) | P2 | **FIXED — flipped 2026-08-04**, verified in source not documents: `tools/lib/migrate-memory.js:1945` opens the fix block naming the bug, and `explainArchiveOutcome` is appended unconditionally at `:1976`. `CHANGELOG.md` `[0.1.18]` § Fixed listed it while this row still read `confirmed` — **the third instance in one release of the fixed-and-never-flipped pattern this file's own footer said was "about to happen again inside the Epic meant to stop it."** Original entry follows. | **`/sig:migrate-memory`'s dry-run prints `0` for its two Epic-only vectors on a linear project, so "could not apply" is byte-identical to "already clean."** `renderDryRun` pushes `vector-3 (closed-Epic evicts): ${v3.evicts.length}` and `archive-tree moves: ${archive.moves.length}` unconditionally (`migrate-memory.js:1931-1932`). On a project that does not use Epic IDs both are **structurally** zero, not incidentally: `planArchiveMoves` filters its input through `EPIC_ID_STRICT_RE` and only matches `.planning/{epicId}-{suffix}.md` (`archive-tree.js:96-110`), and `extractEpicSection` rejects any non-strict ID (`evict.js:175`). If nothing else fires, `noop` goes true (`:1907`) and the whole run reports as a no-op — **a linear project is told the migration is complete when half of it never applied in principle.** **This is `C1`'s exact class in the command next door**, live in the same week M5.E16 shipped the four-status model that fixes it for `/sig:sweep`: a `0` that means *could not look* rendered the same as a `0` that means *checked and clean*. **Found 2026-08-02** reviewing a eval-project-A session report; confirmed by reading the renderer, not by running it. **Fix shape:** apply M5.E16's applicability distinction here — a linear project should read *"not applicable: no Epic-ID'd units in this project"*, never `0`. The missing **capability** (an archive path for linear units) is a separate, Epic-sized item and is filed in `BACKLOG.md`, not here; this entry is only the false-clean report. |
| B72 | `fixed` | **P2** | **`/sig:discuss`'s done-Epic guard — the one that stops a writing command clobbering a finished unit's artifacts — returns `false` for *every* linear-mode project, so it has never been able to fire on 8 of 12 real projects.** Found 2026-08-03 at M5.E18 PLAN research, by reading `isEpicDone`'s body rather than its docblock. `isEpicDone` (`tools/lib/retrospective.js:168`) opens with `if (typeof epicId !== 'string' \|\| !EPIC_ID_STRICT_RE.test(epicId)) return false;` — and `false` is the *"not done, proceed"* answer. So on `eval-project-C` (`current_epic: PHASE12`) or `eval-project-I` (`M1`), the guard evaluates *not done* no matter what is on disk, and `/sig:discuss` without `--epic` proceeds into a completed unit. Its own docblock states the contract it is failing: *"a writing command against a done Epic with no `--epic` must halt rather than clobber that Epic's artifacts"*, and `discuss.md:54` — **the only caller** — spells out the damage: *"it would clobber `{EpicID}-REQUIREMENTS.md`"*. **The strict gate is doing double duty as both a shape check and a verdict**, which is the exact conflation M5.E18 exists to end: `EPIC_ID_STRICT_RE` failing means *"I cannot evaluate this"*, and the code returns *"I evaluated it and the answer is no."* **`B42`'s shape** — a documented mode a whole guard silently does not serve — and **`B53`'s seam** (a non-strict `current_epic` splitting one behaviour in two), now in a third location. Note the asymmetry that hid it: in Epic mode the guard works, and Signal-on-Signal has been Epic-mode since M4.5.E11, so no dogfood run could ever have surfaced it. **Not a regression** — `isEpicDone` has been strict-gated since M4.5.E11.S1.t1, when `EPIC_ID_STRICT_RE` was made the single source of truth; the linear-mode consequence was never derived. **Absorbed into M5.E18 as part of FR5's slice (Brett, 2026-08-03)** rather than filed and deferred: FR5 already rewrites `isEpicDone`'s closure condition for stub retros, so the shape fix and the stub fix land in the same function, in one edit, with one pair of tests. Fixing only the stub half would leave the function still blind to the projects the Epic is being written for. **✅ FIXED 2026-08-04 (M5.E18 S5.t3).** `isEpicDone` now returns `{status: 'done'|'not-done'|'cannot-evaluate', reason}` — a non-strict unit id is `cannot-evaluate`, never the proceed answer. That remains a separate deferred decision, and this row is marked `fixed` for the packaging question only — stated here so the status is not read as answering the positioning one. Detail: `M6.E1-RETROSPECTIVE.md`, `D-M6E1-7`.

**1. There is no include / exclude / files / ignore field. This is a confident "no such field exists," not a failure to find one.** A case-insensitive grep for `"files"`, `"include"`, `"exclude"`, `"ignore"`, `.gitignore` and `.npmignore` across the full reference returns **zero hits**. `commands`/`agents`/`skills` scope what **loads**, not what **copies**. Claude Code *"ignores top-level fields it does not recognize"*, so an invented `"files": [...]` would validate as a warning and silently do nothing.

**2. A subdirectory plugin root is supported and is the only lever.** `"source": "./plugin"` is still the **relative string form**, so `B58`'s lesson survives — `install-contract.test.js:69` asserts `typeof source === 'string'` *and* `toBe('.')`; only the second line changes. Constraint that must be checked before moving anything: *"Copied plugins cannot reference files outside their directory. Paths that traverse outside the plugin root (such as `../shared-utils`) will not work after installation."* `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` becomes the subdirectory, and it is referenced from `tools/`, `hooks/` and **7+ command files**.

**3. The biggest number in the install is not in this row, and the same move fixes it.** Measured: the cached copy is **58 MB, of which `node_modules` is 47 MB** — devDependencies (`vitest`, `eslint`, `esbuild`) on every user's machine. It is not copied; Claude Code **installs** it. Documented trigger: the install *"runs only when the plugin's root directory contains **both** a `package.json` and a supported lockfile"* — and *"You can't turn the automatic install off; no setting or environment variable disables it."* **A plugin root without those two files never triggers it.** Signal has exactly **one** runtime dependency (`yaml`, used by `tools/lib/profile.js` + `state.js`); everything else is dev-only.

**4. ⚠ The move does NOT fix the content half, and this is the finding that matters.** The marketplace and the plugin are **separate fetches**. Adding a git-hosted marketplace clones the marketplace repo **in full** — measured here at **19 MB at `~/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/signal`, `.planning/` included**. No `source` value changes that, because `source` describes the plugin, not the marketplace. **So every packaging fix addresses size and none of them addresses "users receive Signal's working notes."** Removing `.planning/` from what users receive requires either taking it out of the public repo, or decoupling the plugin fetch from the marketplace repo (`git-subdir` against a separate repo, `npm` — whose `files`/`.npmignore` are the only real allowlist anywhere in this system — or `archive` with a CI-built zip + `sha256`). **All three collide head-on with `D-M5E17-4`** (relative `.`, users track `main`, no `ref`/`sha` to drift) and reintroduce a publish step.

**Also measured, not one of the questions asked, and larger than the bug:** `~/.claude/plugins/cache/signal` holds **13 versions totalling 728 MB** — `0.1.5` is still present. Whatever the per-version size becomes, it is multiplied by that.

**Migration deliverable, required in the same release as the packaging change (Brett, 2026-08-14):** an existing-users section on `signal.insightriot.com/install` — *"installed before v0.1.2x? here is how to clear the old copy."* **It cannot be written before the packaging change ships**, because the instruction is *re-add from the new URL* and that URL does not exist yet. **Measured first, and the obvious version of this section would be wrong:** the plugin cache **mostly clears itself**. `~/.claude/plugins/cache/signal/sig` holds 13 versions / 728 MB, but `0.1.6`–`0.1.12` and `0.1.14` are **already gone**, and 11 of the 13 survivors are inside the documented **~14-day orphan grace period** (*"marks the previous version directory as orphaned and removes it in a background sweep roughly 14 days later"*). Telling users to `rm -rf` inside their Claude config for something that self-heals would be bad advice. **Two things are genuinely worth an instruction:** (1) the **marketplace clone** — 19 MB, not version-swept, and orphaned outright by a move to a URL marketplace, so it needs `claude plugin marketplace remove` rather than aging out; (2) `claude plugin prune` is **not** the tool for either — it removes auto-installed *dependencies*, never version directories. **One measured anomaly, stated rather than explained:** `0.1.5` (2026-07-14) is **31 days** old and still present, well past the grace period, cause unknown.

**Bottom line: the size half is small and the content half is a positioning decision.** `.planning/` staying in git is still not in question; only what an install copies — and the answer is that packaging alone cannot stop it while the marketplace source is this repo. The broader *"should `.planning/` be public at all"* question (deferred 2026-08-13) is therefore **load-bearing for this row**, not adjacent to it. |

For F–L none of them are.** The corpus is a live set of directories, so its membership does change — `M5.E10`'s own measurement moved `FR8` from 5 to 4 to 5 in two days for exactly that reason. Every recorded measurement naming a project past `E` is therefore **quietly incomparable across releases**, which is the failure the comment says positional labelling already caused once. *Fix:* derive the letter deterministically from the hash rather than from list position, or pin all 13. Pairs with `B97`, which needs the same decision about which letter each project takes. **FIXED 2026-08-13 (`M5.E10`)** — all 13 pinned by hash in `measure-corpus.js`; a new project takes the next free letter and keeps it, and a departing project does **not** free its letter (reuse would make two projects share a label across releases, which is the whole failure). **Brett's call, recorded:** pin today's mapping and publish the caveat rather than reconstruct `F`–`L` by hand — the original assignment was never recorded and reconstruction would be a guess. `references/eval-corpus.md` now says that references to `F`+ predating this date may not resolve to the same project. **Confirmed live while fixing it:** the mapping moved twice inside ten minutes, and one project shifted `M` → `L` between two runs. |
| B96 | `fixed` | **P2** | **`extractEpicSection` cannot see a heading inside a blockquote, so `evictEpicNarrative` reports `no-section` — *"a safe no-op"* — for a narrative that exists and is 5 KB.** Found 2026-08-13 while validating `M5.E10`'s SHIP preconditions, by dry-running the §5.5 coverage gate rather than waiting for ship to run it. `evict.js:189` builds `` `(?:^|\n)(#{1,6})[ \t]+…` ``, which requires the heading to start the line; Signal's live STATE.md carries its in-flight block as `> ## ▶ IN FLIGHT — M5.E10, opened 2026-08-11`, inside a blockquote. `extractEpicSection` returns `{found: false}`, `evictEpicNarrative` returns `{evicted: false, reason: 'no-section'}`, and `commands/ship.md` §5.5 documents that outcome as *"a safe no-op"*. **It is safe; it is not a no-op.** The consequence is that the closing Epic's narrative is never relocated to `archive/`, so live `STATE.md` accretes every Epic's block forever — precisely what `M5.E1` FR2b built eviction to prevent, and the `STATE.md`-size advisory then fires on growth nothing will drain. **This is `B39`'s shape:** *could not find it* renders identically to *there is nothing to find*. `M5.E19` evicted correctly (`archive/M5/E19/STATE-NARRATIVE.md` exists), so this is a regression in the **document**, not the code — which is exactly why the code should distinguish the two cases. *Fix (design call, not taken here):* either report a fourth outcome when the Epic id appears in the body but no heading matches, or teach the heading regex to skip a `> ` prefix. **Deliberately not fixed inside `M5.E10`** — it is an `M5.E1` module, found at REVIEW-close, and the safe half (the gate refuses rather than corrupting) already holds. *Repro:* `extractEpicSection(parseFrontmatter(STATE.md).body, 'M5.E10')` → `{found:false}` while the body contains the block. **FIXED 2026-08-13 (`M5.E10`).** The heading and boundary patterns accept an optional `> ` prefix. **Fixed in the code rather than by un-blockquoting the document, deliberately: the code should read the shape the maintainer writes, not require the maintainer to write the shape the code reads.** Confirmed end-to-end — the section now resolves at 4562 bytes, and `verifyCardCoverage` then **refused** it, naming six decision ids and one date the retrospective did not carry. That is the R1 safety working: the retro was extended to cover them and the gate now passes, so eviction will actually run at ship. |


## M5.E7's changelog section is invisible to `/sig:update` · **RESOLVED 2026-08-18**

**Status:** resolved-not-a-defect

The heading was relabelled from `## [Unreleased] — 2026-07-26 …` to `## 2026-07-26 — The v2 direction audit (M5.E7) · analysis only, no version cut`, which was the actual defect: a section that said *unreleased* about finished work.

**The invisibility itself turns out to be correct, not a bug.** The entry's own first line says *"No code shipped, so no version was cut."* Nobody updating between two versions ever received this, because there was nothing to receive — so `changelogBetween` skipping it is the right behaviour, and giving it a version number would have invented a release that never happened. That would have been a false published fact, in the file this week's work exists to keep honest.

Closes the matching entry in `OPEN-QUESTIONS.md`.

## Whole-population deny assertion — the shape B81 needs

**Status:** needs-triage

**Approach for `B81`, borrowed from `vercel-labs/eve-software-factory-template` (MIT).** Its eval harness enumerates the whole write-tool population once, in `evals/helpers.ts`, and every read-only eval asserts `notCalledTool` across **all of it** rather than naming the one tool a bad run might reach for. Its own comment states the property: *"a new write tool added to the extension is automatically forbidden in every read-only eval until someone allows it deliberately."*

That is deny-by-default over an enumerated population, and it is exactly the shape `B81` needs. `guard-callers.test.js` today governs **1 of ~25 CLI flags** in `tools/` and its "population is not empty" assertion cannot distinguish that from governing all of them — so the fix is not "detect more flags", it is "assert over the declared population and fail when a member is ungoverned."

Two details worth copying with it: the population list is **kept next to the thing it mirrors** with an explicit sync note naming the source file, and the *exceptions are named individually* with a reason (`read_factory_brain` and `read_artifact` are deliberately absent from the deny list, and the comment says why). An exception with a written reason is auditable; an omission is not.

Reference: `evals/helpers.ts` in that repo. Not a straight port — Signal has no tool-call event stream to assert against — but the population-assertion shape transfers to `tools/` flags directly.

⚠ **It was never assigned the id `B111` in this file** — it was captured as a heading, not a table
row — **while five other documents in the same PR cited `B111` as though it were.** Caught by the
independent reviewer on PR #211, not by the filer.

the default outcome, not an unlucky one.**

(`M6.E5-REQUIREMENTS.md` — the shipped extractor returns **5** ids where **34** exist), and the
observation that the collapse propagates into `checkValidationConsistency`, which reads both halves
of its diff through the same extractor and can therefore only confirm agreement at **group**
granularity. Both are folded into `B100` rather than tracked here.

## `detectProjectKind` calls every non-git directory `greenfield`, so a real codebase is told to start fresh

**Status:** needs-triage

**Status: verified by execution WITH A CONTROL ARM, 2026-08-27.** `detectProjectKind`
returns `greenfield` for **any** directory without a `.git`, however much source it contains — so
`/sig:add`'s missing-`.planning/` error tells the operator of a full codebase to *"start fresh"*
when *"scan the existing code"* is the correct advice.

**The deciding line** (`tools/lib/add.js:192`):

```js
export function detectProjectKind(baseDir) {
  if (!existsSync(join(baseDir, '.git'))) return 'greenfield';   // <-- returns here
  ...
  const hasSource = entries.some(...)                             // <-- dead for non-git dirs
  return hasSource ? 'brownfield' : 'greenfield';
}
```
